statement: In the coordinates of Equation (3.2), almost every s∗ ∈ B has the following two properties. (i) There are a neighborhood B∗ ⊂ B of s∗, a number ε > 0, and a real-analytic map ψ : B∗ × (−ε, ε) → Rk such that ψ(s, 0) = 0, ψ(s, u) ∈ As (s ∈ B∗, 0 < u < ε). (ii) Set E(s, t) = Rk \ t−1 As, d(s, t; v) = min{1, dist(v, E(s, t))}. 9 There is a 1-Lipschitz function d∗ : Rk → [0, 1] such that, for every compact L ⊂ Rk, lim s→s∗ t↓0 sup v∈L |d(s, t; v) − d∗(v)| = 0. (3.4) The set F = {v : d∗(v) = 0} is a closed cone, invariant under every positive real dilation, and 0 ∈ F. In particular, for every sequence sj → s∗, tj ↓ 0, and vj → v, one has d(sj, tj; vj) → d∗(v). If v ∈ F, then dist(vj, E(sj, tj)) −→ 0. If v / ∈ F, some fixed ball about v is contained in t−1 j Asj for all sufficiently large j.
